steps.caption_md: Scanning `nums = [2, 8, -3, 5, 1, 9, -4]` with `k = 3`. Build the first full window once: `2 + 8 + (-3) = 7`. That's our starting `best`.
Slide one step: `5` enters on the right, `2` leaves on the left. `7 + 5 - 2 = 10` — no re-summing of the middle elements. New `best = 10`.
Next slide: `right` moves to index 4 (value `1`). Before anything changes, what does this step do?

predict.prompt_md: The window is `[8, -3, 5]` with `window_sum = 10`. It slides so `1` enters. What is the new `window_sum`, and what happens to `best`?
predict.explanation_md: One element enters (`+1`) and exactly one leaves (`-8`, the old left edge), so the sum is `3`. Forgetting the subtraction would let the window grow past `k`. Re-summing gives the same number but costs O(k) per step — the whole point is the O(1) update. `best` only changes when the new sum beats it.

steps.caption_md: `9` enters and `-3` leaves: `3 + 9 - (-3) = 15`. Removing a negative number *raises* the sum. New `best = 15` for the window `[5, 1, 9]`.
Last slide: `-4` enters, `5` leaves: `15 - 4 - 5 = 6`. The scan is done. Every window has length 3, so the best sum gives the best average: `15 / 3 = 5.0`.
